Both are already linked to 95 common concepts, including equilibrium distribution, collision and atom, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses equilibrium distribution as a bridge: first, review how molecule and power law tail are each currently treated through equilibrium distribution; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
quant-2943-3555.phd: A 3-4 year programme building a unified framework for molecule and power law tail. Year 1: systematic review of the 95 shared concepts (starting with equilibrium distribution, collision and atom); years 2-3: develop and validate a joint method; year 4: generalise it and release open tools and data.
quant-2943-3555.masters: A 6-12 month project: reproduce one recent molecule study and one recent power law tail study, then run a focused experiment combining the two through equilibrium distribution, reporting what transfers and what does not.
